answer: Cross-branch quorum stops sybils: influence grants need approvals from at least three separate invitation subtrees, like three willow roots sharing no soil. Approvals tracing to the same genesis inviter are discarded as correlated, however many pile up. The rule lets approvals wander across branches, admitting only branches with distinct genesis identities per the invitation ledger. An attacker with N clones under one root pays for N audits yet earns one branch's worth of power; the rising tide of fake identities adds nothing, because influence scales with branch count, never headcount.
